1951: Paul Arizin (23) is the game's centre of gravity. Al Cervi is still going at 34. Scores sit around 84 a game. A 10-team league playing 66 games a year. Big men, set shots and no margin for error.
1952: The Lakers wear the crown, but the Royals (41-25) owned the regular season. Keep an eye on Monk Meineke, 22, the brightest young talent. A 10-team league playing 70 games a year. Paul Arizin led the league in scoring last year at 25.4. Big men, set shots and no margin for error.
1953: Lakers hold the title and everyone knows it. Neil Johnston is the one every coach plans around. 9 teams, 72 games. Eddie Miller is 22 and already a problem.
1954: The 24-second shot clock is new. Teams score 95 a night. Keep an eye on Bob Pettit, 22, the brightest young talent. 9 teams, 72 games.
1955: Nationals hold the title and everyone knows it. Keep an eye on Maurice Stokes, 22, the brightest young talent. Father Time keeps losing to Bobby Wanzer, 34. 8 franchises fight for the title over 72 games. Big men, set shots and no margin for error.
1956: Bill Russell arrives in Boston. The Warriors are the team to beat. 8 teams, 72 games. Pace is fast: about 115 possessions a game.
1957: The Celtics are the team to beat. Dolph Schayes (29) is the game's centre of gravity. Last year's scoring crown went to Paul Arizin (25.6 a night). 8 teams, 72 games. Big men, set shots and no margin for error.
1958: The Hawks wear the crown, but the Celtics (49-23) owned the regular season. Bob Pettit is the one every coach plans around. Keep an eye on Hal Greer, 22, the brightest young talent. 8 franchises fight for the title over 72 games.
1959: Everyone is chasing the Celtics. Wilt Chamberlain (23) is the game's centre of gravity. Keep an eye on Rudy LaRusso, 22, the brightest young talent. 8 teams, 75 games. Big men, set shots and no margin for error.
1960: The Celtics come in as defending champions. All eyes on Wilt Chamberlain, the best player alive right now. 8 franchises fight for the title over 79 games. Keep an eye on Oscar Robertson, 22, the brightest young talent.
1961: Chicago expands the league to nine. Walt Bellamy is 22 and already a problem. Pace is fast: about 128 possessions a game. 9 franchises fight for the title over 80 games. The Celtics cast a long shadow over everyone else.
1962: Everyone is chasing the Celtics. Keep an eye on Terry Dischinger, 22, the brightest young talent. 9 franchises fight for the title over 80 games. Teams score 115 a night.
1963: Wilt Chamberlain (27) is the game's centre of gravity. 9 franchises fight for the title over 80 games. Teams score 111 a night. Keep an eye on Art Heyman, 22, the brightest young talent.
1964: Oscar Robertson (26) is the game's centre of gravity. Pace is fast: about 120 possessions a game. Willis Reed is 22 and already a problem. 9 teams, 80 games.
1965: The Celtics are the team to beat. All eyes on Wilt Chamberlain, the best player alive right now. A 9-team league playing 80 games a year. Teams score 116 a night.
1966: The Bulls arrive. Rick Barry is 22 and already a problem. Richie Guerin is still going at 34. 10 franchises fight for the title over 81 games.
1967: Seattle and San Diego join the league. All eyes on Wilt Chamberlain, the best player alive right now. A 12-team league playing 82 games a year. Rick Barry led the league in scoring last year at 35.6.
1968: Milwaukee and Phoenix join. Keep an eye on Wes Unseld, 22, the brightest young talent. Father Time keeps losing to Elgin Baylor, 34. 14 teams, 82 games. The Celtics cast a long shadow over everyone else.
1969: The Celtics wear the crown, but the Bullets (57-25) owned the regular season. 14 franchises fight for the title over 82 games. Keep an eye on Kareem Abdul-Jabbar, 22, the brightest young talent. Teams score 117 a night.
1970: Cleveland, Buffalo and Portland join. Pace is fast: about 116 possessions a game. Keep an eye on Calvin Murphy, 22, the brightest young talent. 17 teams, 82 games.
1971: The Bucks are the team to beat. A 17-team league playing 82 games a year. Father Time keeps losing to Wilt Chamberlain, 35. Spencer Haywood is 22 and already a problem. Afros, ABA flair and a league finding its feet.
1972: The Lakers are the team to beat. 17 teams, 82 games. Keep an eye on Phil Chenier, 22, the brightest young talent. Father Time keeps losing to Wilt Chamberlain, 36.
1973: All eyes on Kareem Abdul-Jabbar, the best player alive right now. A 17-team league playing 82 games a year. Teams score 106 a night. Last year's scoring crown went to Tiny Archibald (34.0 a night). Afros, ABA flair and a league finding its feet.
1974: The Celtics wear the crown, but the Bucks (59-23) owned the regular season. Scores sit around 103 a game. John Drew is 20 and already a problem. A 18-team league playing 82 games a year.
1975: The Warriors wear the crown, but the Celtics (60-22) owned the regular season. 18 franchises fight for the title over 82 games. Last year's scoring crown went to Bob McAdoo (34.5 a night). Teams score 104 a night.
1976: Four ABA clubs join the NBA. The Celtics wear the crown, but the Warriors (59-23) owned the regular season. 22 franchises fight for the title over 82 games. Bob McAdoo led the league in scoring last year at 31.1. Afros, ABA flair and a league finding its feet.
1977: 22 teams, the ABA is gone, and Larry Bird is coming. Boston will draft him next June and wait. Scoring crown: Gervin and Thompson, down to the last night.
1978: Bird is drafted and waiting. A year from now Magic Johnson enters the draft, and a coin flip decides who gets him. Rewrite how it lands.
1979: The three-point line is new. Magic Johnson and Larry Bird are rookies, and the league is about to change forever.
1980: Dallas joins as the 23rd team. Boston has just landed Robert Parish and Kevin McHale. Magic's Lakers are the champions to catch.
1981: Isiah Thomas is a rookie in Detroit. Bird's Celtics and Dr. J's 76ers circle each other, and in November Pat Riley takes over the Lakers.
1982: Moses Malone joins Philadelphia and promises 'Fo, Fo, Fo'. Ralph Sampson and Clyde Drexler are in next June's draft.
1983: The 1984 draft is the greatest ever: Hakeem, Jordan, Barkley, Stockton. Every bad team is thinking about it. Does yours tank?
1984: Michael Jordan is a rookie in Chicago. Hakeem Olajuwon, Charles Barkley and John Stockton are in the same class. Patrick Ewing's lottery is coming.
1985: The first draft lottery sent Patrick Ewing to New York. Bird's Celtics head for 67 wins and Jordan breaks his foot in week one.
1986: Michael Jordan is about to average 37 points a night. The Bad Boy Pistons are coming for everyone, and the Lakers still have Magic.
1987: Jordan wins MVP and Defensive Player of the Year in one season. Dominique Wilkins duels him at the dunk contest. Detroit is closing in.
1988: Charlotte and Miami join as the 24th and 25th teams. Detroit's Jordan Rules are about to start working.
1989: Orlando and Minnesota arrive, 27 teams. Phil Jackson is the Bulls' coach and Jordan has a young Scottie Pippen beside him.
1990: Jordan finally gets past Detroit, and Magic's Lakers meet him in the Finals. Rewrite the first Bulls title.
1991: In November Magic Johnson walks away from basketball. Next summer a Dream Team goes to Barcelona, and Shaquille O'Neal enters the draft.
1992: Shaq is a rookie in Orlando, Alonzo Mourning in Charlotte. Jordan is on a three-peat and might be tired of it.
1993: Jordan retires and plays baseball. Hakeem's Rockets and Patrick Ewing's Knicks are the favourites. Who wins without him?
1994: A fax that says 'I'm back'. Michael Jordan returns in March. Toronto and Vancouver join next season.
1995: Toronto and Vancouver join as the 28th and 29th teams. The Bulls will go 72-10, and a teenager named Kevin Garnett is a rookie.
1996: Kobe Bryant, Allen Iverson, Steve Nash and Ray Allen are rookies. Shaq joins the Lakers. Jordan's Bulls are still on top.
1997: The Last Dance. The Spurs drafted Tim Duncan after a lost year, and the Bulls' coach is on his way out.
1998: A lockout cuts the season to 50 games. Michael Jordan retires again and the Spurs, with Duncan, are the new force.
1999: Shaq and Kobe have Phil Jackson, and the Lakers are about to win three in a row. Portland is heading for a Game 7 collapse.
2000: The Lakers are champions. Allen Iverson will drag Philadelphia to the Finals, and the draft features high-schooler Kwame Brown.
2001: The Kings are about to take the Lakers to a seven-game series that people still argue over. Yao Ming enters the draft next June.
2002: The Lakers have three-peated, but familiar threats are on the horizon: Duncan's Spurs, the Kings and Dallas. A high-school kid named LeBron James is the pick every bad team wants.
2003: LeBron, Carmelo, Wade and Bosh are rookies. The Lakers add Karl Malone and Gary Payton. Can Detroit stop them?
2004: On November 19 the Pacers and Pistons brawl in the stands at Auburn Hills. The Malice at the Palace changes two teams for good.
2005: Hurricane Katrina sends the Hornets to Oklahoma City. In January Kobe Bryant scores 81 against Toronto.
2006: Greg Oden or Kevin Durant? A draft with two franchise players is coming, and Miami wants another ring.
2007: Garnett and Ray Allen join Paul Pierce in Boston. The Sonics are playing their last season in Seattle.
2008: The Sonics become the Thunder, with Durant and Westbrook. LeBron's Cavaliers go 66-16. Blake Griffin is in the draft.
2009: Everyone is waiting for July 2010: LeBron, Wade, Bosh and Amar'e can all walk. The league is about to be rewritten.
2010: LeBron took his talents to South Beach. Miami's Big Three is built, and a lockout is looming.
2011: A lockout cuts the season to 66 games. Jeremy Lin is about to start a craze, and Chris Paul is headed to Los Angeles.
2012: Days before opening night Oklahoma City trades James Harden. Miami is chasing a second title, and the Spurs are lurking.
2013: Philadelphia is tanking for the future with 'The Process'. Wiggins, Parker and Embiid are in the draft. The Spurs want revenge.
2014: LeBron has gone home to Cleveland. Steve Kerr is the new coach in Golden State, and Stephen Curry is about to become MVP.
2015: The Warriors are chasing 73 wins. Kobe plays his last season, and a 3-1 lead in the Finals is not safe.
2016: Kevin Durant joins the 73-win Warriors. Russell and Westbrook averages a triple-double. Cleveland's champions are on the clock.
2017: Kyrie Irving is a Celtic, Chris Paul joins Harden in Houston, and LeBron's contract is running down.
2018: LeBron is a Laker, Kawhi a Raptor. Zion Williamson is the most hyped college player in years, and bad teams are thinking about him.
2019: Kawhi goes to the Clippers, Durant to Brooklyn. In March the world stops: Covid ends the season in a bubble in Orlando.
2020: A 72-game season after the pandemic, with empty arenas. Giannis is chasing a title and James Harden is looking to leave Houston.
2021: Ben Simmons won't play in Philadelphia, Kyrie won't play in Brooklyn, and Golden State's old core is healthy again.
2022: Kevin Durant wants out of Brooklyn. Nikola Jokic's Nuggets are rising, and Victor Wembanyama is the draft everyone is tanking for.
2023: The first NBA Cup is in December. Wembanyama is a rookie in San Antonio, and Boston wants number 18.
2024: The Celtics are champions. Luka Doncic is about to be traded in a way nobody sees coming, and Cooper Flagg is the next big draft.
2025: Opening night of 2025-26. Cooper Flagg is a rookie in Dallas and Oklahoma City carry the crown. Play it, then step into the future.
2026: This is the present day. From here the real NBA ends and the future is yours to write. Real rosters, made-up people to come.
